reviewer: Claude 2, independent; did not author the subject
discipline: Refute, do not confirm. v12 is a remasurement successor, not a repair successor: the world moved between v11 and v12. HEAD advanced from e160bc44 to cf18ed04, D-247 recorded g21-fixture-corpus.v8, and eight per-D-002-platform copies of the two D-245 CC-5 payloads now exist on disk. That shape dictated the attack. The characteristic failure of a repair successor is a cosmetic repair; the characteristic failure of a REMASUREMENT successor is the inverse — a stale carry-forward, a sentence that was true of v11's world and is now false of v12's, surviving unrevised because it was copied rather than remeasured. The second characteristic failure is overcorrection: a remasurement that, having correctly retired one remainder, quietly retires more than the world actually discharged, or converts a staleness measurement into a closure claim. The review was therefore run as five attacks. First, custody was re-derived from primary sources and never inherited from any predecessor's verdict: every path-plus-sha256 pair anywhere in the document was recomputed from disk, every recordedInputs entry was recomputed, every cited commit was resolved in git and its subject line read, the live register was read for the DR-G21 status token, the owner cell and required-now, and the four frozen predecessors named by the dispatch were reproduced at their pinned digests and modes. Second, a full structural diff was taken between frozen v11 and the subject, flattened to leaf paths, so that the delta could be inspected as a closed set rather than sampled as prose — the governing question being whether every change is attributable to D-247 and whether anything changed that D-247 does not license. Third, the two quotations the dispatch makes load-bearing were compared against their live sources as bytes, not as paraphrase: occupancy v4's 692-character passProperty and corpus v8's authoredCatalog.executionRemains. Fourth, a stale-carry-forward sweep was run over the whole document, splitting every string into sentences and surfacing every sentence that mentions CC-5 copies, to test each one for tense and truth against the post-corpus-v8 world. Fifth, the enumerations the subject presents as measurements — namedCorpusWhenFixturesExist, the remaining-CC-5-injection list, and the platform provenance — were compared structurally against the live artifacts they claim to consume, because an enumeration is where an invented list would hide.
decisionRule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. No MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX stand, so the verdict is ACCEPT.
codexStanding: No Codex review of this v12 subject was read, no directory listing filtered for one was taken, and no part of this verdict is informed by the other reviewer of this subject. Two disclosures, stated precisely rather than glossed. First, the frozen Claude 2 review of the PREDECESSOR v11 was read in full. That file is a pinned predecessor cited by digest in the subject's own basedOn.predecessorV11.reviews.claude and in recordedInputs, and it reproduces its recorded digest. It was read because this dispatch forbids inventing a finding schema, and it is the authoritative statement of the established schema for this lineage; it also carries the prior landed-finding record that a remasurement successor must not regress. It is a frozen predecessor artifact, not knowledge of any reviewer's position on this v12. Second, the custody audit computed sha256 over every file the subject cites, and that set includes frozen Codex reviews of predecessor artifacts. Those files were opened only as bytes by a hashing routine; no Codex review file's contents were rendered, displayed or read at any point in this review, and the audit consumed only the resulting hex digests. The frozen Codex verdict STRINGS for predecessors were read where the subject itself recites them in its own basedOn block, which is the subject's text under review, not the other reviewer's file.

acceptanceStatement: The subject is a correct and tightly scoped remasurement successor. The world moved exactly once between v11 and v12 — D-247 recorded corpus v8, authoring eight per-D-002-platform copies of the two D-245 CC-5 payloads — and the subject remeasures exactly that and nothing else. The delta was inspected as a closed set rather than sampled: two removals, both correct retirements of work D-247 performed; one added disclaimer; and a set-wise comparison confirming that no disclaimer or commitment was lost under the index shifts. Every operative measurement field is byte-identical to frozen v11, so the leftover posture did not drift where the world did not move. The retirement is measured, not declared: the CC-5-copy remainder is called stale as an authoring claim while leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded stays empty and OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING stays leftoverDesign true, preserving the remaining CC-5 injections, the ten live-cell classes, CC-1 through CC-4, CC-6 through CC-11, NT-6 and FC-NC-CA1-PROCESS-TREE. The stale-carry-forward sweep found no surviving sentence that D-247 falsified; the one v11 sentence at risk was rewritten into an attributed historical statement plus a current remasurement. Both load-bearing quotations reproduce against live bytes: occupancy v4's 692-character passProperty is carried verbatim with 'on every D-002 platform' intact, and corpus v8's authoredCatalog.executionRemains is recited in its four-item form including EV-5 diagnostic/audit bytes at all five sites. No platform list is minted; the eight platform-indexed paths are measurements of bytes corpus v8 authored, matching its own counts and the live tree exactly, with provenance faithfully attributed to G10 occupancy v2. Custody reproduces completely: 133 citation checks across 73 recorded inputs and 61 inline digest pairs, zero mismatches and zero missing; six cited commits resolved against their decision headings; the file 08 pin, the live OPEN status token, the live owner cell, the live corpus structure and required-now 28. All six prior landed findings remain landed and none regressed. No MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX stand.
